docs.title: Outlier Detection and Treatment Strategy
docs.text:
Systematic Outlier Identification: Statistical analysis identified extreme values in three continuous variables requiring intervention:

  • DurationOfPitch: 2 observations exceeding 40 minutes (likely data entry errors)

  • MonthlyIncome: 4 observations outside 12,000-40,000 range (extreme economic outliers)

  • NumberOfTrips: 4 observations exceeding 10 annual trips (likely business travelers or data errors)

Treatment Rationale: Rather than imputation or transformation, complete removal was chosen because:

  • Low Impact: Affected observations represent <0.2% of total dataset

  • Data Quality: Extreme values likely represent measurement errors rather than legitimate business insights

  • Model Stability: Outlier removal prevents model distortion by extreme cases

Business Impact Assessment: Outlier removal improves model generalization to typical customer populations while maintaining data integrity for mainstream customer segments.

docs.title: Missing Value Imputation Strategy
docs.text:
Categorical Variable Imputation: Mode imputation applied to categorical variables based on business logic:

  • TypeofContact: Most frequent contact method reflects standard operational procedure

  • PreferredPropertyStar: Modal preference represents typical customer expectations

  • NumberOfChildrenVisiting: Mode imputation accounts for family travel patterns

Continuous Variable Imputation: Median imputation selected for continuous variables due to:

  • Robustness: Median remains stable despite skewed distributions

  • Business Logic: Median represents typical customer characteristics better than mean

  • Distribution Preservation: Maintains underlying data distribution patterns

Data Leakage Prevention: Imputation parameters calculated exclusively from training data and applied to validation/test sets, ensuring no information leakage from future data into model training.

docs.title: Feature Engineering Decisions
docs.text:
Variable Exclusion Strategy: Four variables removed from modeling due to temporal availability constraints:

  • DurationOfPitch: Unavailable before customer contact

  • NumberOfFollowups: Represents post-contact interaction

  • ProductPitched: Sales strategy decision, not customer characteristic

  • PitchSatisfactionScore: Post-interaction feedback unavailable during prediction

Exclusion Rationale: The model must predict purchase likelihood before initial customer contact, requiring exclusion of any post-contact interaction variables.

Categorical Encoding Implementation: One-hot encoding applied to categorical variables with drop_first=True to prevent multicollinearity while preserving categorical information for model interpretation.

docs.title: Data Splitting Strategy
docs.text:
Stratified Sampling Approach: 70-30 train-test split with stratification ensures:

  • Class Balance Preservation: Maintains 18% purchase rate in both sets

  • Representative Sampling: Both sets reflect overall population characteristics

  • Robust Evaluation: Test set provides unbiased performance estimation

Validation Strategy Considerations: Single train-test split chosen over cross-validation due to sufficient sample size (4,888 observations) and need for consistent final model evaluation.

docs.title: Feature Scaling Considerations
docs.text:
SVM-Specific Scaling: MinMax scaling (-1 to 1 range) applied specifically for Support Vector Machine algorithms due to:

  • Distance-Based Sensitivity: SVM performance depends on feature scale uniformity

  • Optimization Efficiency: Scaled features improve convergence speed

  • Numerical Stability: Prevents large-scale features from dominating decision boundaries

Tree-Based Model Advantage: Decision Tree and Random Forest models require no scaling due to their split-based decision mechanisms being scale-invariant.

docs.title: Preprocessing Pipeline Validation
docs.text:
Quality Assurance Checks: Post-preprocessing validation confirms:

  • Zero Missing Values: All variables complete across train/test sets

  • Consistent Encoding: Categorical variables properly transformed

  • Data Type Alignment: Numerical variables properly formatted for modeling

  • Shape Consistency: Feature dimensionality matches across datasets

docs.title: Preprocessing Limitations
docs.text:
Information Loss: Outlier removal eliminates potentially valuable edge cases that might represent high-value customer segments or unique market opportunities.

Imputation Assumptions: Mode and median imputation assumes missing data patterns are random rather than systematic, which may not hold for sensitive variables like income.

Feature Reduction Impact: Exclusion of post-contact variables limits model's ability to learn from complete customer interaction history, potentially reducing predictive power.

Temporal Static Assumption: Preprocessing assumes customer characteristics remain stable over time, which may not reflect evolving customer preferences or life circumstances.

[See Code Walkthrough Section 4: Data Preprocessing Pipeline Implementation]

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Algorithm Selection Strategy
docs.text:
Four classification algorithms were selected to capture different aspects of customer purchase behavior:

Logistic Regression: Linear baseline model for interpretable probability estimation

Support Vector Machine: Non-linear pattern recognition with kernel flexibility

Decision Tree: Rule-based interpretation with clear decision pathways

Random Forest: Ensemble method for improved generalization and feature importance

docs.title: Evaluation Metrics Framework
docs.text:
Primary Metric: Recall (Sensitivity) Business priority focuses on maximizing recall because:

  • False Negative Cost: Missing a potential buyer represents lost revenue (entire package value)

  • False Positive Cost: Contacting a non-buyer costs only marketing resources

  • Business Impact: Revenue opportunity cost significantly exceeds marketing cost

Supporting Metrics: Precision, F1-Score, and accuracy provide balanced performance assessment while maintaining recall priority.

docs.title: Logistic Regression Performance Analysis
docs.text:
Baseline Performance: - Training Accuracy: 82% with perfect specificity but poor recall (25%)

  • Test Performance: Similar pattern with 23% recall, indicating consistent underperformance in identifying buyers

Threshold Optimization Results: Precision-Recall curve analysis identified optimal threshold of 0.25, improving:

  • Recall Enhancement: From 23% to 67% (+44% improvement)

  • Precision Trade-off: Decreased from higher baseline but maintained business-acceptable levels

  • Business Impact: Significantly improved buyer identification capability

Model Interpretation: Linear decision boundary may be insufficient for complex customer behavior patterns, suggesting need for non-linear approaches.

docs.title: Support Vector Machine Analysis
docs.text:
Linear Kernel Limitations: Initial SVM with linear kernel and default threshold showed catastrophic failure:

  • Complete Class Blindness: Predicted all customers as non-buyers (0% recall)

  • Imbalanced Data Impact: Class imbalance caused model to default to majority class

  • Threshold Sensitivity: Default 0.5 threshold inappropriate for imbalanced classification

Threshold Optimization Impact: Optimal threshold of 0.25 dramatically improved performance:

  • Recall Recovery: From 0% to 61% with threshold adjustment

  • Generalization: Similar performance on train/test sets indicating good generalization

  • F1-Score Improvement: From 0.00 to 0.52 demonstrating balanced performance recovery

RBF Kernel Enhancement: Non-linear RBF kernel with optimized threshold (0.17) achieved:

  • Superior Recall: 69% recall representing best performance among tested models

  • Balanced Metrics: Maintained reasonable precision while maximizing recall

  • Business Applicability: Optimal performance for business objective of maximizing buyer identification

docs.title: Decision Tree Performance Evaluation
docs.text:
Default Model Overfitting: Unpruned decision tree exhibited classic overfitting symptoms:

  • Perfect Training Performance: Near 100% accuracy on training data

  • Generalization Failure: Significant performance degradation on test set

  • Complexity Overreach: Model memorized training patterns rather than learning generalizable rules

Hyperparameter Tuning Results: GridSearchCV optimization with 5-fold cross-validation found optimal parameters:

  • Complexity Control: max_depth, max_leaf_nodes, min_samples_split tuning

  • Overfitting Reduction: Improved generalization through pruning

  • Performance Balance: Better test performance with slight training performance reduction

Feature Importance Insights: Tuned decision tree identified key predictive features:

  • MonthlyIncome: Primary decision factor

  • Age: Secondary demographic influence

  • NumberOfTrips: Behavioral pattern significance

docs.title: Random Forest Ensemble Performance
docs.text:
Initial Performance Assessment: Random Forest showed typical ensemble behavior:

  • Training Excellence: Near-perfect training performance indicating high model capacity

  • Overfitting Tendency: Performance gap between train/test sets

  • Moderate Recall: 47% recall below SVM performance

Feature Importance Validation: Random Forest confirmed decision tree insights regarding important features:

  • Income Dominance: Monthly income as primary predictive factor

  • Age Significance: Demographic importance validation

  • Trip Behavior: Travel history predictive value

Ensemble Limitations: Despite reputation for overfitting resistance, Random Forest showed:

  • Insufficient Recall: Below business requirements for buyer identification

  • Tuning Necessity: Default parameters inadequate for imbalanced classification

docs.title: Model Comparison Synthesis
docs.text:
Performance Ranking by Recall: 1. SVM with RBF Kernel: 69% recall (optimal for business objective) 2. Logistic Regression: 67% recall (close second with better interpretability) 3. SVM with Linear Kernel: 61% recall (threshold-dependent improvement) 4. Random Forest: 47% recall (below business requirements) 5. Decision Tree: Variable recall with overfitting concerns

Business Model Selection: SVM with RBF kernel emerges as optimal choice based on:

  • Highest Recall: Best buyer identification capability
  • Balanced Performance: Reasonable precision maintenance
  • Generalization: Consistent train/test performance
  • Business Alignment: Maximizes revenue opportunity identification

docs.title: Critical Model Limitations
docs.text:
Imbalanced Data Challenge: All models struggled with severe class imbalance (18% purchase rate), requiring threshold optimization rather than architectural solutions.

Feature Engineering Gaps: Limited feature engineering may have constrained model performance, particularly interaction terms or derived features.

Cross-Validation Absence: Single train-test split may not provide robust performance estimates compared to k-fold cross-validation approaches.

Ensemble Exploration: Limited exploration of advanced ensemble methods (XGBoost, stacking) that might achieve superior performance.

[See Code Walkthrough Section 5: Model Implementation & Comprehensive Comparison]

↩ Back to Top

docs.title: Threshold Optimization Methodology
docs.text:
Precision-Recall Curve Analysis: Systematic threshold optimization employed precision-recall curves to identify optimal operating points for each model, prioritizing recall maximization while maintaining business-acceptable precision levels.

Business-Driven Threshold Selection: Threshold selection considered business cost structure:

  • Revenue Opportunity Cost: Missing a buyer costs entire package revenue

  • Marketing Cost: Contacting non-buyer costs limited marketing resources

  • ROI Optimization: Threshold balances recall gains against precision losses

docs.title: Logistic Regression Optimization
docs.text:
Threshold Sensitivity Analysis: Comprehensive threshold testing from 0.1 to 0.9 revealed:

  • Optimal Point: 0.25 threshold providing 67% recall with acceptable precision

  • Trade-off Curve: Clear inverse relationship between precision and recall

  • Business Sweet Spot: 0.25 represents optimal business ROI balance

Performance Improvement Quantification: - Recall Enhancement: 44 percentage point improvement (23% → 67%)

  • Revenue Impact: Potential to identify 67% of buyers versus 23% with default threshold

  • Customer Reach: Expanded targetable customer segment significantly

docs.title: Support Vector Machine Optimization Journey
docs.text:
Linear Kernel Recovery: Initial catastrophic failure (0% recall) completely recovered through threshold optimization:

  • Threshold Impact: 0.25 threshold enabled 61% recall achievement

  • Class Balance Resolution: Addressed severe imbalanced data effects

  • Performance Validation: Consistent train/test performance confirmed generalization

RBF Kernel Enhancement: Advanced to non-linear RBF kernel with aggressive threshold optimization:

  • Optimal Threshold: 0.17 (lower than linear kernel) for maximum recall

  • Performance Peak: 69% recall representing best overall model performance

  • Non-Linear Advantage: RBF kernel captured complex customer behavior patterns

  • Business Champion: Selected as final model for deployment

docs.title: Decision Tree Hyperparameter Tuning
docs.text:
GridSearchCV Implementation: Comprehensive parameter space exploration included:

  • max_depth: Range 1-100 with 10-unit steps for complexity control

  • max_leaf_nodes: [50, 75, 150, 250] for terminal node limitation

  • min_samples_split: [10, 30, 50, 70] for split threshold control

  • Cross-Validation: 5-fold CV for robust parameter evaluation

Overfitting Mitigation: Tuning successfully reduced overfitting through:

  • Complexity Reduction: Optimal parameters prevented training data memorization

  • Generalization Improvement: Better test set performance with controlled training performance

  • Interpretability Maintenance: Pruned tree remained business-interpretable

Optimal Configuration Results: Best parameters achieved balanced performance while maintaining decision tree interpretability advantages for business stakeholder communication.

docs.title: Feature Importance Analysis
docs.text:
Consistent Ranking Validation: Both Decision Tree and Random Forest confirmed identical feature importance ranking:

  1. MonthlyIncome: Dominant predictive factor indicating economic capacity primacy

  2. Age: Secondary demographic influence reflecting life stage travel patterns

  3. NumberOfTrips: Behavioral indicator of travel propensity and experience

Business Intelligence Validation: Feature importance results align with tourism industry knowledge:

  • Economic Capacity: Income directly relates to travel affordability

  • Life Stage: Age correlates with discretionary spending and travel motivation

  • Travel Experience: Previous trip frequency indicates travel comfort and interest

docs.title: Model Selection Rationale
docs.text:
SVM RBF Kernel Selection: Final model selection based on comprehensive evaluation:

  • Primary Objective: Highest recall (69%) maximizing buyer identification

  • Generalization: Consistent performance across train/test sets

  • Business Alignment: Optimal revenue opportunity maximization

  • Robustness: Effective handling of imbalanced classification challenge

Alternative Model Considerations: - Logistic Regression: Close second with 67% recall and superior interpretability

  • Decision Tree: High interpretability but lower recall performance

  • Random Forest: Insufficient recall for business requirements

docs.title: Optimization Limitations and Risks
docs.text:
Threshold Dependency: Heavy reliance on threshold optimization rather than algorithmic improvements may indicate:

  • Feature Engineering Gaps: Insufficient feature development for inherent performance

  • Data Quality Issues: Underlying data limitations requiring threshold compensation

  • Model Architecture: Possible need for more sophisticated modeling approaches

Overfitting Risk: Aggressive threshold optimization on validation data may lead to:

  • Test Set Overfit: Optimized thresholds may not generalize to new data

  • Performance Degradation: Real-world performance may fall below validation estimates

  • Business Impact: Production model may underperform expectations

Class Imbalance Persistence: Despite optimization efforts, fundamental class imbalance challenges remain:

  • Minority Class Complexity: 18% purchase rate creates inherent modeling difficulty

  • Data Collection: May require additional data collection strategies

  • Sampling Techniques: Advanced techniques (SMOTE, ensemble sampling) unexplored

docs.title: Production Deployment Considerations
docs.text:
Model Monitoring Requirements: Optimized models require continuous monitoring for:

  • Threshold Drift: Performance degradation due to changing customer behavior

  • Feature Distribution Changes: Input data evolution affecting model validity

  • Business Metric Tracking: Actual recall/precision in production environment

A/B Testing Framework: Production deployment should include controlled testing comparing optimized model against baseline approaches to validate real-world business impact.

[See Code Walkthrough Section 6: Advanced Optimization & Threshold Tuning]

docs.title: Comprehensive Feature Importance Analysis
docs.text:
Cross-Model Validation: Feature importance rankings demonstrated remarkable consistency across both Decision Tree and Random Forest models, providing strong validation for business insights:

Primary Predictive Factors:

  1. MonthlyIncome (Dominant Factor)
  2. Statistical Significance: Highest importance score across all tree-based models
  3. Business Logic: Direct correlation with discretionary spending capacity for travel
  4. Customer Segmentation: Enables income-based targeting strategies

  5. Package Customization: Informs price point optimization for different income segments

  6. Age (Secondary Demographic Factor)

  7. Life Stage Correlation: Reflects travel motivation and lifestyle priorities
  8. Spending Pattern: Indicates discretionary income availability and time flexibility
  9. Target Demographics: Validates focus on 25-50 age segment for optimal conversion

  10. Marketing Messaging: Enables age-appropriate communication strategies

  11. NumberOfTrips (Behavioral Indicator)

  12. Travel Propensity: Indicates comfort level and interest in travel experiences
  13. Experience Factor: Higher trip frequency suggests travel sophistication
  14. Upselling Potential: Experienced travelers more likely to purchase premium packages
  15. Loyalty Indicators: Frequent travelers represent high-value customer segment

docs.title: Business Intelligence Implications
docs.text:
Customer Segmentation Strategy: Feature importance analysis enables sophisticated customer segmentation:

High-Value Segment Characteristics: - Income Range: Upper-middle income brackets with highest conversion probability - Age Demographics: 30-45 age range representing peak earning and travel years - Travel Experience: 3+ annual trips indicating established travel behavior

Medium-Value Segment Identification: - Emerging Earners: Younger customers with growing income potential - Occasional Travelers: 1-2 annual trips with upselling opportunities - Geographic Expansion: Tier 2 city customers with untapped potential

Low-Priority Segment Recognition: - Income Constraints: Lower income segments requiring different value propositions - Age Extremes: Very young or senior customers with different travel motivations - Non-Travelers: Zero-trip customers requiring foundational travel interest development

docs.title: Marketing Strategy Optimization
docs.text:
Income-Based Targeting: Primary feature importance of income enables refined marketing approaches:

Premium Package Positioning: - Target: High-income customers (>35,000 monthly income) - Messaging: Luxury, exclusivity, premium experiences - Channels: High-end travel publications, luxury lifestyle platforms

Value Package Marketing: - Target: Middle-income customers (20,000-35,000 monthly income) - Messaging: Value, family-friendly, memorable experiences - Channels: Social media, family-oriented publications

Accessibility Packages: - Target: Lower-income segments with payment flexibility - Messaging: Affordable, payment plans, basic experiences - Channels: Mass market advertising, promotional campaigns

docs.title: Product Development Insights
docs.text:
Package Design Implications: Feature importance guides product development priorities:

Age-Specific Customization: - Young Adults (25-35): Adventure, social experiences, group discounts - Middle Age (35-50): Family packages, comfort, convenience features - Experience-Based: Packages designed for different travel experience levels

Income-Aligned Offerings: - Tiered Pricing: Multiple price points matching income distributions - Value Engineering: Different feature sets for different economic segments - Payment Flexibility: Installment options for income-constrained segments

docs.title: Competitive Advantage Development
docs.text:
Data-Driven Differentiation: Feature importance analysis provides competitive advantages:

Precision Targeting: - Resource Efficiency: Focus marketing spend on high-probability segments - Conversion Optimization: Tailor offerings to predictive characteristics - Customer Experience: Relevant communications based on likelihood factors

Market Expansion: - Underserved Segments: Identify profitable customer groups missed by competitors - Geographic Opportunities: Tier 2 city expansion based on demographic patterns - Product Innovation: Develop packages addressing specific customer characteristic combinations

docs.title: Feature Engineering Opportunities
docs.text:
Derived Feature Potential: Current analysis suggests opportunities for enhanced feature engineering:

Income-Age Interaction: - Life Stage Economics: Combine age and income for life stage-specific targeting - Earning Trajectory: Age-adjusted income for career progression insights - Discretionary Spending: Income minus estimated obligations based on age/family status

Travel Behavior Patterns: - Trip Frequency Trends: Analysis of trip frequency changes over time - Travel Sophistication Index: Combine trip frequency with property preferences - Experience Progression: Model travel experience evolution patterns

docs.title: Business Risk Assessment
docs.text:
Feature Dependency Risks: Heavy reliance on income and age creates business vulnerabilities:

Economic Sensitivity: - Recession Impact: Income-based targeting vulnerable to economic downturns - Market Volatility: Income fluctuations affect customer targeting accuracy - Inflation Effects: Income thresholds may require regular recalibration

Demographic Limitations: - Market Saturation: Over-reliance on specific age segments limits growth - Aging Customer Base: Need for continuous younger customer acquisition - Lifestyle Changes: Evolving travel preferences may shift importance factors

docs.title: Performance Monitoring Strategy
docs.text:
Feature Importance Tracking: Production model requires continuous monitoring of feature importance stability:

Importance Drift Detection: - Monthly Analysis: Track feature importance changes over time - Seasonal Adjustments: Account for seasonal travel pattern variations - Economic Indicators: Monitor correlation with economic condition changes

Model Recalibration Triggers: - Importance Threshold Changes: >10% importance shift triggers model review - New Feature Emergence: Monitor for new predictive factors - Performance Degradation: Declining recall/precision indicates importance evolution

[See Code Walkthrough Section 7: Feature Importance Analysis & Business Translation]

docs.title: Strategic Customer Targeting Framework
docs.text:
Primary Target Segment Optimization: Based on model insights, "Visit with us" should prioritize customers with the following characteristics:

High-Conversion Profile: - Monthly Income: 25,000-40,000 range representing optimal economic capacity - Age Range: 30-45 years indicating peak travel propensity and financial stability - Travel Experience: 2+ annual trips demonstrating established travel behavior - Passport Ownership: International travel capability for wellness tourism packages - Marital Status: Single/unmarried customers showing higher conversion rates

Business Impact Projection: Targeting this optimized segment could improve conversion rates from the current 18% baseline to an estimated 35-45% based on model performance, representing a potential 94-150% increase in package sales efficiency.

docs.title: Product Portfolio Realignment
docs.text:
Package Development Strategy: Current analysis reveals significant misalignment between product pitch frequency and conversion success:

Basic Package Emphasis: - Current Status: Highest conversion rate but underutilized in sales pitches - Recommendation: Increase Basic package pitch frequency by 40% - Revenue Impact: Higher volume through improved conversion rates - Customer Satisfaction: Better price-value alignment for target demographic

Standard Package Repositioning: - Current Gap: Higher conversion than Deluxe but lower pitch frequency - Strategy: Develop Standard package as primary offering for middle-income segment - Value Proposition: Enhanced features without premium pricing - Market Position: Sweet spot between affordability and experience quality

Deluxe Package Refinement: - Current Challenge: High pitch frequency but lower conversion rates - Recommendation: Reposition for high-income segment with enhanced value proposition - Target Refinement: Focus on customers with 35,000+ monthly income - Feature Enhancement: Add exclusive experiences justifying premium pricing

docs.title: Geographic Expansion Strategy
docs.text:
Tier 2 City Market Development: Analysis reveals significant untapped potential in Tier 2 cities:

Market Gap Identification: - Current Distribution: 65% Tier 1, 8% Tier 2, 27% Tier 3 - Opportunity: Tier 2 cities underrepresented despite economic potential - Strategic Focus: Develop targeted Tier 2 city marketing campaigns

Expansion Implementation: - Phase 1: Market research in top 10 Tier 2 cities - Phase 2: Pilot marketing campaigns with localized messaging - Phase 3: Regional office establishment for sustained presence - Success Metrics: Target 15% customer base from Tier 2 cities within 2 years

docs.title: Sales Process Optimization
docs.text:
Contact Strategy Refinement: Current random contact approach shows significant inefficiency:

Predictive Targeting Implementation: - Model Deployment: Use SVM RBF model for prospect scoring - Threshold Application: Contact customers with >0.17 probability score - Resource Allocation: Focus sales efforts on high-probability prospects - Efficiency Gain: Estimated 69% buyer identification rate versus current random approach

Follow-up Strategy Enhancement: - Data-Driven Follow-ups: Increase follow-up frequency for high-scoring prospects - Personalized Messaging: Tailor communication based on customer characteristics - Timing Optimization: Develop optimal contact timing based on customer profiles

docs.title: Wellness Tourism Package Launch Strategy
docs.text:
Target Customer Identification: For the new Wellness Tourism Package, prioritize customers with:

Primary Characteristics: - Health-Conscious Demographics: Age 30-50 with higher income levels - Travel Experience: 3+ annual trips indicating openness to new experiences - International Capability: Passport ownership for global wellness destinations - Economic Capacity: Income levels supporting premium wellness experiences

Launch Phase Implementation: - Soft Launch: Target top 20% of model-scored customers - Feedback Collection: Gather customer response data for product refinement - Iterative Improvement: Adjust package features based on initial customer feedback - Scale-up: Expand to broader customer segments based on initial success

docs.title: Customer Lifecycle Management
docs.text:
Retention Strategy Development: Beyond acquisition, focus on customer lifecycle value:

Experience Progression: - First-Time Buyers: Ensure exceptional experience to drive repeat purchases - Repeat Customers: Offer graduated experiences matching travel sophistication - Loyalty Programs: Develop rewards system for frequent travelers - Referral Incentives: Leverage satisfied customers for word-of-mouth marketing

# Defining the hist_box() function
def hist_box(data, col):
    """
    Combined histogram and boxplot visualization for comprehensive univariate analysis

    Parameters:
    -----------
    data : DataFrame
        Input dataset containing the variable to analyze
    col : str
        Column name to visualize

    Returns:
    --------
    matplotlib figure with boxplot (top) and histogram (bottom) subplots
    """
    f, (ax_box, ax_hist) = plt.subplots(
        2, sharex=True, 
        gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': (0.15, 0.85)}, 
        figsize=(12, 6)
    )

    # Adding boxplot with mean indicator
    sns.boxplot(data=data, x=col, ax=ax_box, showmeans=True)

    # Adding histogram with KDE
    sns.histplot(data=data, x=col, kde=True, ax=ax_hist)

    plt.show()

Purpose: Creates standardized visualization combining distribution shape (histogram) and summary statistics (boxplot) for comprehensive univariate analysis.

Flow: - Subplot Layout: 2-row layout with shared x-axis for consistent scaling - Boxplot: Top panel shows quartiles, outliers, and mean - Histogram: Bottom panel shows distribution shape with KDE overlay - Integration: Shared x-axis enables direct comparison between views

Impact: Standardizes analysis approach across all variables, revealing both distributional properties and outlier patterns simultaneously.

# Defining the stacked_barplot() function
def stacked_barplot(data, predictor, target, figsize=(10,6)):
    """
    Creates stacked bar plot showing target variable distribution across predictor categories

    Parameters:
    -----------
    data : DataFrame

    target : str

    )

Impact: Enables complete case analysis for modeling while maintaining data integrity. Alternative deletion would lose valuable observations.

# Creating metric function
def metrics_score(actual, predicted):
    """
    Comprehensive classification performance evaluation

    Parameters:
    -----------
    actual : array-like
        True class labels
    predicted : array-like  
        Predicted class labels

    Returns:
    --------
    Prints classification report and confusion matrix visualization
    """
    print(classification_report(actual, predicted))

    cm = confusion_matrix(actual, predicted)
    plt.figure(figsize=(8,5))

    sns.heatmap(cm, annot=True, fmt='.2f')
    plt.ylabel('Actual')
    plt.xlabel('Predicted')
    plt.show()

Purpose: Standardizes performance evaluation across all models with comprehensive metrics and visualization.

Flow: - Classification Report: Precision, recall, F1-score for each class - Confusion Matrix: Visual representation of prediction accuracy - Heatmap Visualization: Clear display of true/false positives/negatives

Impact: Ensures consistent evaluation methodology enabling direct model comparison. Visual confusion matrix helps identify specific error patterns.

docs.title: Threshold Optimization for Logistic Regression
docs.text:
# Predict_proba gives the probability of each observation belonging to each class
y_scores_lg = lg.predict_proba(X_train)

# Generate precision-recall curve
precisions_lg, recalls_lg, thresholds_lg = precision_recall_curve(y_train, y_scores_lg[:,1])

# Plot values of precisions, recalls, and thresholds
plt.figure(figsize=(10,7))
plt.plot(thresholds_lg, precisions_lg[:-1], 'b--', label='precision')
plt.plot(thresholds_lg, recalls_lg[:-1], 'g--', label='recall')
plt.xlabel('Threshold')
plt.legend(loc='upper left')
plt.ylim([0,1])
plt.show()

# Setting the optimal threshold
optimal_threshold = 0.25

# Evaluate with optimal threshold
y_pred_train = lg.predict_proba(X_train)
metrics_score(y_train, y_pred_train[:,1] > optimal_threshold)

y_pred_test = lg.predict_proba(X_test)
metrics_score(y_test, y_pred_test[:,1] > optimal_threshold)

Purpose: Optimizes decision threshold to maximize recall for business objective of identifying potential buyers.

Flow: - Probability Generation: Extract class probabilities instead of hard predictions - Curve Analysis: Plot precision-recall trade-off across thresholds - Threshold Selection: Choose threshold optimizing business objective (recall) - Re-evaluation: Assess performance with optimized threshold

Impact: Dramatically improves recall from 23% to 67% (+44 percentage points) by optimizing threshold for business objective rather than statistical default.

def analyze_precision_recall_curve(model, X_train, y_train, model_name):
    """
    Comprehensive precision-recall analysis for threshold optimization

    Parameters:
    -----------
    model : sklearn estimator
        Trained classification model with predict_proba method
    X_train : DataFrame/array
        Training features
    y_train : Series/array
        Training target variable
    model_name : str
        Model identifier for plotting

    Returns:
    --------
    dict : Optimal threshold and performance metrics
    """
    # Generate probability predictions
    y_scores = model.predict_proba(X_train)[:, 1]

    # Calculate precision-recall curve
    precisions, recalls, thresholds = precision_recall_curve(y_train, y_scores)

    # Plot precision-recall curve
    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))
    plt.plot(thresholds, precisions[:-1], 'b--', label='Precision', linewidth=2)
    plt.plot(thresholds, recalls[:-1], 'g--', label='Recall', linewidth=2)
    plt.xlabel('Threshold', fontsize=12)
    plt.ylabel('Score', fontsize=12)
    plt.title(f'Precision-Recall Curve: {model_name}', fontsize=14)
    plt.legend(loc='upper right', fontsize=11)
    plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
    plt.ylim([0, 1])
    plt.show()

    # Find optimal threshold for business objective (maximize recall with acceptable precision)
    f1_scores = 2 * (precisions[:-1] * recalls[:-1]) / (precisions[:-1] + recalls[:-1])

    # Business logic: prioritize recall but maintain minimum precision of 0.3
    viable_thresholds = thresholds[precisions[:-1] >= 0.3]
    viable_recalls = recalls[:-1][precisions[:-1] >= 0.3]

    if len(viable_thresholds) > 0:
        optimal_idx = np.argmax(viable_recalls)
        optimal_threshold = viable_thresholds[optimal_idx]
    else:
        # If no threshold meets precision requirement, choose best F1 score
        optimal_idx = np.argmax(f1_scores)
        optimal_threshold = thresholds[optimal_idx]

    return {
        'optimal_threshold': optimal_threshold,
        'precision_at_optimal': precisions[:-1][optimal_idx],
        'recall_at_optimal': recalls[:-1][optimal_idx],
        'f1_at_optimal': f1_scores[optimal_idx]
    }

Purpose: Provides systematic framework for threshold optimization balancing business requirements (recall) with acceptable precision levels.

Flow: - Probability Generation: Extract class probabilities for threshold analysis - Curve Calculation: Generate precision-recall trade-off curves - Visualization: Plot trade-off relationships for stakeholder communication - Business Logic: Apply business constraints (minimum precision) to threshold selection - Optimization: Select threshold maximizing recall within business constraints

Impact: Transforms statistical model outputs into business-optimized decision systems. Framework enables consistent optimization across all models.

def evaluate_model_with_threshold(model, X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test, threshold, model_name):
    """
    Comprehensive model evaluation using optimized threshold

    Parameters:
    -----------
    model : sklearn estimator
        Trained model
    X_train, X_test : DataFrame/array
        Training and test features
    y_train, y_test : Series/array
        Training and test targets
    threshold : float
        Optimized decision threshold
    model_name : str
        Model identifier

    Returns:
    --------
    dict : Comprehensive performance metrics
    """
    # Training set evaluation
    train_probs = model.predict_proba(X_train)[:, 1]
    train_preds = (train_probs > threshold).astype(int)

    # Test set evaluation
    test_probs = model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]
    test_preds = (test_probs > threshold).astype(int)

    # Calculate comprehensive metrics
    from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, precision_score, recall_score, f1_score, roc_auc_score

    results = {
        'model_name': model_name,
        'threshold': threshold,
        'train_accuracy': accuracy_score(y_train, train_preds),
        'train_precision': precision_score(y_train, train_preds),
        'train_recall': recall_score(y_train, train_preds),
        'train_f1': f1_score(y_train, train_preds),
        'train_auc': roc_auc_score(y_train, train_probs),
        'test_accuracy': accuracy_score(y_test, test_preds),
        'test_precision': precision_score(y_test, test_preds),
        'test_recall': recall_score(y_test, test_preds),
        'test_f1': f1_score(y_test, test_preds),
        'test_auc': roc_auc_score(y_test, test_probs)
    }

    return results

# Evaluate all models with optimal thresholds
final_results = []
for model_name, config in models_config.items():
    print(f"\n=== Final Evaluation: {model_name} ===")

    result = evaluate_model_with_threshold(
        config['model'],
        config['data'][0],
        config['data'][1],
        y_train,
        y_test,
        config['optimal_threshold'],
        model_name
    )

    final_results.append(result)

    # Display key metrics
    print(f"Test Recall: {result['test_recall']:.3f}")
    print(f"Test Precision: {result['test_precision']:.3f}")
    print(f"Test F1 Score: {result['test_f1']:.3f}")
    print(f"Test AUC: {result['test_auc']:.3f}")

def calculate_business_impact(results_df, baseline_conversion_rate=0.18, package_value=1000, marketing_cost=50):
    """
    Calculates projected business impact of model deployment

    Parameters:
    -----------
    results_df : DataFrame
        Model comparison results
    baseline_conversion_rate : float
        Current random targeting conversion rate
    package_value : float
        Average package revenue
    marketing_cost : float
        Cost per customer contact

    Returns:
    --------
    DataFrame : Business impact analysis
    """
    impact_analysis = []

    for _, model in results_df.iterrows():
        model_name = model['model_name']
        test_recall = model['test_recall']
        test_precision = model['test_precision']

        # Calculate business metrics
        # Assume 1000 potential customers
        total_customers = 1000
        actual_buyers = int(total_customers * baseline_conversion_rate)  # 180 actual buyers

        # Model performance
        identified_buyers = int(actual_buyers * test_recall)  # Buyers identified by model
        total_contacted = int(identified_buyers / test_precision)  # Total customers contacted

        # Revenue calculation
        revenue_captured = identified_buyers * package_value
        marketing_costs = total_contacted * marketing_cost
        net_revenue = revenue_captured - marketing_costs

        # Baseline comparison (random targeting)
        baseline_contacted = total_customers  # Contact everyone randomly
        baseline_buyers_found = actual_buyers  # Find all buyers but at high cost
        baseline_revenue = baseline_buyers_found * package_value
        baseline_costs = baseline_contacted * marketing_cost
        baseline_net = baseline_revenue - baseline_costs

        # Improvement metrics
        cost_reduction = (baseline_costs - marketing_costs) / baseline_costs
        efficiency_gain = (identified_buyers / total_contacted) / baseline_conversion_rate

        impact_analysis.append({
            'model': model_name,
            'identified_buyers': identified_buyers,
            'total_contacted': total_contacted,
            'conversion_rate': identified_buyers / total_contacted,
            'revenue_captured': revenue_captured,
            'marketing_costs': marketing_costs,
            'net_revenue': net_revenue,
            'cost_reduction_pct': cost_reduction * 100,
            'efficiency_gain_x': efficiency_gain,
            'vs_baseline_net': net_revenue - baseline_net
        })

    return pd.DataFrame(impact_analysis)

# Calculate business impact
business_impact = calculate_business_impact(comparison_df)
print("\n=== Business Impact Analysis ===")
print(business_impact.round(2))

def extract_feature_importance(models_dict, feature_names):
    """

    Parameters:
    -----------
    models_dict : dict
        Dictionary of trained models
    feature_names : list
        List of feature names

    Returns:
    --------
    DataFrame : Feature importance comparison across models
    """
    importance_data = {}

    # Decision Tree importance
    if 'decision_tree' in models_dict:
        dt_importance = models_dict['decision_tree'].feature_importances_
        importance_data['Decision_Tree'] = dt_importance

    # Random Forest importance
    if 'random_forest' in models_dict:
        rf_importance = models_dict['random_forest'].feature_importances_
        importance_data['Random_Forest'] = rf_importance

    # Logistic Regression coefficients (absolute values as proxy for importance)
    if 'logistic_regression' in models_dict:
        lg_coef = np.abs(models_dict['logistic_regression'].coef_[0])
        # Normalize to 0-1 scale for comparison
        lg_importance = lg_coef / np.sum(lg_coef)
        importance_data['Logistic_Regression'] = lg_importance

    # Create comparison DataFrame
    importance_df = pd.DataFrame(importance_data, index=feature_names)
    importance_df = importance_df.fillna(0)  # Fill any missing values

    # Calculate average importance across models
    importance_df['Average'] = importance_df.mean(axis=1)

    # Sort by average importance
    importance_df = importance_df.sort_values('Average', ascending=False)

    return importance_df

    ax1.set_ylabel('Features', fontsize=12)

    # 2. Model comparison heatmap
    model_cols = [col for col in top_features.columns if col != 'Average']
    sns.heatmap(top_features[model_cols].T, 
                annot=True, fmt='.3f', 
                cmap='Blues', ax=ax2)
    ax2.set_title('Feature Importance by Model Type', fontsize=14)
    ax2.set_xlabel('Features', fontsize=12)

    # Emerging Travelers Segment
    emerging_mask = (
        (df['MonthlyIncome'] >= income_med) & (df['MonthlyIncome'] < income_high) &

class TravelPackagePredictionSystem:
    """
    Production-ready travel package purchase prediction system

    Attributes:
    -----------
    model : sklearn estimator
        Trained classification model
    threshold : float
        Optimized decision threshold
    feature_names : list
        Expected feature names for input validation
    preprocessing_pipeline : dict
        Preprocessing steps and parameters
    performance_baseline : dict
        Baseline performance metrics for monitoring
    """

    def __init__(self, model, threshold, feature_names, preprocessing_pipeline, baseline_metrics):
        self.model = model
        self.threshold = threshold
        self.feature_names = feature_names
        self.preprocessing_pipeline = preprocessing_pipeline
        self.baseline_metrics = baseline_metrics
        self.prediction_log = []
        self.performance_history = []

    def validate_input_data(self, customer_data):
        """
        Validates input customer data for prediction

        Parameters:
        -----------
        customer_data : DataFrame
            Customer information for prediction

        Returns:
        --------
        bool : True if valid, raises exception if invalid
        """
        # Check required columns
        missing_cols = set(self.feature_names) - set(customer_data.columns)
        if missing_cols:
            raise ValueError(f"Missing required columns: {missing_cols}")

        # Check data types
        numeric_cols = ['Age', 'MonthlyIncome', 'NumberOfTrips', 'NumberOfPersonVisiting', 
                       'PreferredPropertyStar', 'NumberOfChildrenVisiting', 'Passport', 'OwnCar']

        for col in numeric_cols:
            if col in customer_data.columns:
                if not pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(customer_data[col]):
                    raise ValueError(f"Column {col} must be numeric")

        # Business logic validation
        if 'Age' in customer_data.columns:
            invalid_ages = (customer_data['Age'] < 18) | (customer_data['Age'] > 100)
            if invalid_ages.any():
                raise ValueError("Age must be between 18 and 100")

        if 'MonthlyIncome' in customer_data.columns:
            invalid_income = customer_data['MonthlyIncome'] < 0
            if invalid_income.any():
                raise ValueError("Monthly income cannot be negative")

        return True

    def preprocess_customer_data(self, customer_data):
        """
        Applies preprocessing steps to customer data

        Parameters:
        -----------
        customer_data : DataFrame
            Raw customer data

        Returns:
        --------
        DataFrame : Preprocessed data ready for prediction
        """
        processed_data = customer_data.copy()

        # Handle missing values using training-derived parameters
        if 'median_imputer' in self.preprocessing_pipeline:
            median_cols = self.preprocessing_pipeline['median_imputer']['columns']
            median_values = self.preprocessing_pipeline['median_imputer']['values']

            for col, median_val in zip(median_cols, median_values):
                if col in processed_data.columns:
                    processed_data[col].fillna(median_val, inplace=True)

        if 'mode_imputer' in self.preprocessing_pipeline:
            mode_cols = self.preprocessing_pipeline['mode_imputer']['columns']
            mode_values = self.preprocessing_pipeline['mode_imputer']['values']

            for col, mode_val in zip(mode_cols, mode_values):
                if col in processed_data.columns:
                    processed_data[col].fillna(mode_val, inplace=True)

        # Apply categorical encoding
        if 'categorical_encoding' in self.preprocessing_pipeline:
            encoded_features = self.preprocessing_pipeline['categorical_encoding']['feature_names']

            # Create dummy variables for categorical columns
            categorical_cols = ['TypeofContact', 'Occupation', 'Gender', 'MaritalStatus', 'Designation', 'CityTier']

            for col in categorical_cols:
                if col in processed_data.columns:
                    dummies = pd.get_dummies(processed_data[col], prefix=col, drop_first=True)
                    processed_data = pd.concat([processed_data, dummies], axis=1)
                    processed_data.drop(columns=[col], inplace=True)

        # Ensure all required features are present
        for feature in self.feature_names:
            if feature not in processed_data.columns:
                processed_data[feature] = 0  # Add missing encoded features as 0

        # Reorder columns to match training data
        processed_data = processed_data[self.feature_names]

        return processed_data

    def predict_purchase_probability(self, customer_data):
        """
        Predicts purchase probability for new customers

        Parameters:
        -----------
        customer_data : DataFrame
            Customer information

        Returns:
        --------
        dict : Prediction results with business insights
        """
        # Validate and preprocess input
        self.validate_input_data(customer_data)
        processed_data = self.preprocess_customer_data(customer_data)

        # Generate predictions
        probabilities = self.model.predict_proba(processed_data)[:, 1]
        predictions = (probabilities > self.threshold).astype(int)

        # Calculate confidence scores
        confidence_scores = np.where(
            predictions == 1,
            probabilities,  # For positive predictions, confidence = probability
            1 - probabilities  # For negative predictions, confidence = 1 - probability
        )

        # Create results
        results = []
        for i in range(len(customer_data)):
            customer_result = {
                'customer_id': i,
                'purchase_probability': round(probabilities[i], 3),
                'predicted_purchase': bool(predictions[i]),
                'confidence_score': round(confidence_scores[i], 3),
                'risk_level': self.categorize_risk_level(probabilities[i]),
                'recommended_action': self.get_recommendation(probabilities[i], predictions[i]),
                'segment': self.identify_customer_segment(customer_data.iloc[i])
            }
            results.append(customer_result)

        # Log predictions for monitoring
        self.log_predictions(customer_data, results)

        return results

    def categorize_risk_level(self, probability):
        """Categorizes customer risk level based on purchase probability"""
        if probability >= 0.7:
            return "High Conversion Risk"
        elif probability >= 0.4:
            return "Medium Conversion Risk"
        elif probability >= 0.2:
            return "Low Conversion Risk"
        else:
            return "Very Low Conversion Risk"

    def get_recommendation(self, probability, prediction):
        """Provides business recommendation based on prediction"""
        if prediction == 1 and probability >= 0.7:
            return "High Priority: Contact with premium package offerings"
        elif prediction == 1 and probability >= 0.4:
            return "Medium Priority: Contact with standard package offerings"
        elif probability >= 0.2:
            return "Low Priority: Include in broad marketing campaigns"
        else:
            return "Very Low Priority: Focus resources on higher probability customers"

    def identify_customer_segment(self, customer_row):
        """Identifies customer segment based on characteristics"""
        income = customer_row.get('MonthlyIncome', 0)
        age = customer_row.get('Age', 0)
        trips = customer_row.get('NumberOfTrips', 0)

        if income >= 30000 and 30 <= age <= 50 and trips >= 3:
            return "High-Value Travelers"
        elif income >= 20000 and age < 35 and trips >= 1:
            return "Emerging Travelers"
        else:
            return "Budget-Conscious"

    def log_predictions(self, input_data, results):
        """Logs predictions for performance monitoring"""
        log_entry = {
            'timestamp': pd.Timestamp.now(),
            'customer_count': len(input_data),
            'high_probability_count': sum(1 for r in results if r['purchase_probability'] >= 0.5),
            'predictions_made': len(results)
        }
        self.prediction_log.append(log_entry)

Purpose: Provides complete production-ready system for deploying travel package prediction model with comprehensive validation, preprocessing, and business logic.

Flow: - Input Validation: Ensures data quality and business rule compliance - Preprocessing: Applies training-derived transformations consistently - Prediction Generation: Produces probability scores and binary predictions - Business Translation: Converts technical outputs to actionable recommendations - Performance Logging: Tracks system usage for monitoring and optimization

Impact: Enables reliable production deployment with automatic quality assurance, business-relevant outputs, and performance tracking capabilities.

def create_customer_scoring_api():

    """
    from typing import List, Dict, Any
    import json

    # Initialize prediction system (would use actual trained model in production)
    prediction_system = TravelPackagePredictionSystem(
        model=svm_rbf,  # Best performing model
        threshold=0.17,  # Optimal threshold
        feature_names=list(X_train.columns),
        preprocessing_pipeline={
            'median_imputer': {
                'columns': ['Age', 'MonthlyIncome', 'NumberOfTrips'],
                'values': [37.0, 25000.0, 2.0]  # Example values from training
            },
            'mode_imputer': {
                'columns': ['TypeofContact', 'PreferredPropertyStar', 'NumberOfChildrenVisiting'],
                'values': ['Self Inquiry', 3, 0]  # Example values from training
            }
        },
        baseline_metrics={'recall': 0.69, 'precision': 0.45, 'f1': 0.55}
    )

    def score_customer(customer_data: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Scores individual customer for purchase likelihood

        Parameters:
        -----------
        customer_data : dict
            Customer information dictionary

        Returns:
        --------
        dict : Scoring results with recommendations
        """
        try:
            # Convert to DataFrame
            customer_df = pd.DataFrame([customer_data])

            # Generate prediction
            results = prediction_system.predict_purchase_probability(customer_df)

            return {
                'status': 'success',
                'customer_score': results[0],
                'timestamp': pd.Timestamp.now().isoformat()
            }

        except Exception as e:
            return {
                'status': 'error',
                'error_message': str(e),
                'timestamp': pd.Timestamp.now().isoformat()
            }

    def score_customer_batch(customers_data: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Scores batch of customers for purchase likelihood

        Parameters:
        -----------
        customers_data : list
            List of customer information dictionaries

        Returns:
        --------
        list : Batch scoring results
        """
        try:
            # Convert to DataFrame
            customers_df = pd.DataFrame(customers_data)

            # Generate predictions
            results = prediction_system.predict_purchase_probability(customers_df)

            return {
                'status': 'success',
                'batch_size': len(customers_data),
                'results': results,
                'summary': {
                    'high_probability_customers': len([r for r in results if r['purchase_probability'] >= 0.5]),
                    'recommended_contacts': len([r for r in results if r['predicted_purchase']]),
                    'average_probability': np.mean([r['purchase_probability'] for r in results])
                },
                'timestamp': pd.Timestamp.now().isoformat()
            }

        except Exception as e:
            return {
                'status': 'error',
                'error_message': str(e),
                'timestamp': pd.Timestamp.now().isoformat()
            }

    return {
        'score_customer': score_customer,
        'score_customer_batch': score_customer_batch,
        'prediction_system': prediction_system
    }

docs.title: Problem Context
docs.text:
Hospital resource management represents one of healthcare's most critical operational challenges, particularly highlighted during the COVID-19 pandemic. The inability to accurately predict patient length of stay (LOS) leads to:

  • Inefficient bed allocation and resource distribution

  • Suboptimal staff scheduling

  • Revenue losses due to operational inefficiencies

  • Potential patient safety risks from inadequate resource planning

HealthPlus hospital faces these exact challenges, experiencing significant losses in both revenue and patient outcomes due to inefficient management systems.

docs.title: Analytical Objective
docs.text:
This tutorial develops a machine learning solution to predict patient length of stay using admission data and initial test results. The analysis addresses two primary questions:

  1. Predictive Modeling: Can we accurately predict LOS using available admission data?

  2. Factor Analysis: Which patient and hospital characteristics most strongly influence length of stay?

docs.title: Methodological Approach
docs.text:
The analysis employs a comprehensive ensemble learning strategy, comparing multiple regression algorithms to identify the optimal predictive model. This approach recognizes that healthcare prediction problems often benefit from different algorithmic perspectives.

Key Performance Criteria: - Prediction accuracy (RMSE, MAE) - Model interpretability for clinical application - Computational efficiency for real-time deployment - Robustness across different patient populations

[See Code Walkthrough Section 1: Environment Setup]

docs.title: Dataset Characteristics
docs.text:
The analysis utilizes a comprehensive dataset of 500,000 patient admission records from HealthPlus hospital. This substantial sample size enables robust statistical analysis while presenting computational challenges that inform model selection decisions.

Data Scope: - Temporal Coverage: Historical admission records for discharged patients only - Feature Diversity: 15 variables covering patient demographics, medical conditions, and hospital operational metrics - Target Variable: Length of stay measured in days (3-51 day range)

docs.title: Critical Data Limitations
docs.text:
Several important limitations affect the analysis scope and generalizability:

  1. Selection Bias: Dataset includes only patients who were actually admitted, excluding emergency department visits that resulted in discharge

  2. Temporal Constraints: No information about seasonal variations or year-over-year trends

  3. Missing Clinical Detail: Limited information about specific treatments, complications, or discharge criteria

  4. Hospital-Specific: Results may not generalize to hospitals with different patient populations or operational structures

docs.title: Feature Categories Analysis
docs.text:
The dataset encompasses four primary feature categories:

Patient Demographics: Age groups, gender - providing basic population stratification

Medical Factors: Severity of illness, health conditions, type of admission - capturing clinical complexity

Operational Variables: Available rooms, staff availability, department assignments - reflecting hospital capacity constraints

Financial Indicators: Insurance status, admission deposits - potentially reflecting socioeconomic factors affecting care decisions

docs.title: Data Quality Assessment
docs.text:
Initial data exploration reveals several positive quality indicators:

  • No Missing Values: Complete dataset with 500,000 fully populated records
  • No Duplicate Records: Each admission represents a unique episode of care
  • Reasonable Value Ranges: All variables fall within expected clinical and operational parameters

However, the analysis identifies potential outliers, particularly in visitor counts (up to 32 visitors) and length of stay (up to 51 days), requiring careful consideration during model development.

docs.title: Distribution Analysis Insights
docs.text:
The exploratory analysis reveals several critical patterns that inform subsequent modeling decisions:

Length of Stay Distribution: - Central Tendency: Median LOS of 9 days with mean around 10 days - Skewness: Right-skewed distribution indicating most patients have shorter stays - Outlier Consideration: Very few patients stay beyond 40 days, suggesting these may represent complex cases or different care pathways

Operational Capacity Patterns: - Room Availability: Average of 3 rooms available, ranging from 0 to 24 - Staffing Levels: Average of 5 available staff members, varying from 0 to 10 - Capacity Constraints: Zero availability scenarios suggest periods of high demand that may affect care quality

docs.title: Departmental Analysis
docs.text:
The analysis reveals significant departmental variation with important implications:

Gynecology Department Dominance: - Handles 68.7% of all admissions - Predominantly serves female patients (74.2% of total patient population) - Generally shorter length of stay compared to other departments

Surgical and Critical Care: - Surgery department represents only 1% of admissions but likely higher complexity - Ward A concentrates the most severe cases with longest stays - Clear correlation between illness severity and departmental assignment

docs.title: Patient Population Characteristics
docs.text:
Age Distribution Insights: - Peak admissions in 21-50 age group (75% of patients) - Elderly (51-100) and pediatric (1-10) patients show longest average stays - Age-related care complexity appears to drive length of stay patterns

Admission Type Analysis: - Trauma cases dominate (62% of admissions) - Emergency and urgent cases combine for 89.3% of total admissions - Planned admissions represent minority, suggesting hospital primarily serves acute care needs

docs.title: Correlation Analysis Results
docs.text:
The correlation analysis yields a surprising finding: minimal linear correlation between continuous variables and length of stay. This suggests:

  1. Non-linear Relationships: LOS prediction may require algorithms capable of capturing complex interactions

  2. Categorical Feature Importance: Departmental assignments, severity classifications, and other categorical variables likely drive prediction accuracy

  3. Ensemble Approach Justification: Multiple algorithms may capture different aspects of the prediction problem

docs.title: Ward-Level Operational Insights

docs.text:
The analysis implements a comprehensive ensemble learning approach, comparing six distinct regression algorithms. This strategy addresses the uncertainty about which algorithmic approach will best capture the complex relationships in healthcare data.

Tree-Based Methods Focus: The emphasis on tree-based algorithms (Decision Trees, Random Forest, Bagging) reflects several healthcare-specific advantages:

  • Interpretability: Clinical stakeholders can understand decision pathways
  • Non-linear Relationship Capture: Ability to model complex interactions between medical factors

Boosting Algorithm Inclusion: AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost provide complementary approaches:

docs.title: Feature Engineering Approach
docs.text:
The analysis employs one-hot encoding for categorical variables, creating a high-dimensional feature space. This approach has both advantages and limitations:

Advantages: - Preserves all categorical information without imposing ordinal relationships - Enables algorithms to learn department-specific or condition-specific patterns - Maintains interpretability of individual factor contributions

Limitations: - Increased dimensionality may lead to curse of dimensionality issues - Potential for overfitting with limited samples per category - Computational complexity increases with feature count

Temporal Validation Concerns: - Random splitting may not reflect real-world deployment where models predict future patients - Seasonal patterns or temporal trends could affect generalizability

Stratification Considerations: - Random splitting across rare conditions or departments may create training-test imbalances - Particularly important given the dominance of gynecology department

docs.title: Cross-Validation Implementation

def comprehensive_quality_assessment(df):
    """
    Detailed data quality analysis with multiple checks

    Parameters:
    df (DataFrame): Input dataset

    Returns:
    dict: Comprehensive quality metrics
    """
    quality_report = {}

    # Missing value analysis
    missing_stats = df.isnull().sum()
    quality_report['missing_values'] = {
        'total_missing': missing_stats.sum(),
        'columns_with_missing': (missing_stats > 0).sum(),
        'missing_percentage': (missing_stats.sum() / (df.shape[0] * df.shape[1])) * 100
    }

    # Data type analysis
    quality_report['data_types'] = {
        'numeric_columns': len(df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns),
        'categorical_columns': len(df.select_dtypes(include=['object']).columns),
        'datetime_columns': len(df.select_dtypes(include=['datetime']).columns)
    }

    # Uniqueness analysis
    unique_stats = {}
    for col in df.columns:
        unique_stats[col] = {
            'unique_count': df[col].nunique(),
            'unique_percentage': (df[col].nunique() / len(df)) * 100
        }
    quality_report['uniqueness'] = unique_stats

    # Outlier detection for numeric columns
    numeric_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns
    outlier_stats = {}
    for col in numeric_cols:
        Q1 = df[col].quantile(0.25)
        Q3 = df[col].quantile(0.75)
        IQR = Q3 - Q1
        lower_bound = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
        upper_bound = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
        outliers = ((df[col] < lower_bound) | (df[col] > upper_bound)).sum()
        outlier_stats[col] = {
            'outlier_count': outliers,
            'outlier_percentage': (outliers / len(df)) * 100
        }
    quality_report['outliers'] = outlier_stats

    return quality_report

# Apply comprehensive assessment
quality_metrics = comprehensive_quality_assessment(data)

def histogram_boxplot(data, feature, figsize=(12, 7), kde=False, bins=None):
    """
    Combined boxplot and histogram visualization

    Parameters:
    data (DataFrame): Input dataset
    feature (str): Column name to visualize
    figsize (tuple): Figure size
    kde (bool): Whether to show density curve
    bins (int): Number of histogram bins

    Purpose: Provides comprehensive view of distribution including
    central tendency, spread, and shape characteristics
    """
    f2, (ax_box2, ax_hist2) = plt.subplots(
        nrows=2,
        sharex=True,
        gridspec_kw={"height_ratios": (0.25, 0.75)},
        figsize=figsize,
    )

    # Boxplot with mean indicator
    sns.boxplot(data=data, x=feature, ax=ax_box2, showmeans=True, color="violet")

    # Histogram with optional KDE
    if bins:
        sns.histplot(data=data, x=feature, kde=kde, ax=ax_hist2, bins=bins, palette="winter")
    else:
        sns.histplot(data=data, x=feature, kde=kde, ax=ax_hist2)

    # Add central tendency lines
    ax_hist2.axvline(data[feature].mean(), color="green", linestyle="--", label="Mean")
    ax_hist2.axvline(data[feature].median(), color="black", linestyle="-", label="Median")
    ax_hist2.legend()

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

# Analyze target variable distribution
histogram_boxplot(data, "Stay (in days)", kde=True, bins=30)

def stacked_barplot(data, predictor, target):
    """
    Stacked bar chart for categorical relationships

    Parameters:
    data (DataFrame): Input dataset
    predictor (str): Independent categorical variable
    target (str): Dependent variable for stacking

    Purpose: Visualizes relationships between categorical variables
    with both counts and proportions
    """
    count = data[predictor].nunique()
    sorter = data[target].value_counts().index[-1]

    # Create cross-tabulation with margins
    tab1 = pd.crosstab(data[predictor], data[target], margins=True).sort_values(
        by=sorter, ascending=False
    )
    print("Cross-tabulation with counts:")
    print(tab1)
    print("-" * 120)

    # Create proportional cross-tabulation
    tab = pd.crosstab(data[predictor], data[target], normalize="index").sort_values(
        by=sorter, ascending=False
    )

    # Create stacked bar plot
    tab.plot(kind="bar", stacked=True, figsize=(count + 1, 5))
    plt.legend(loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1))
    plt.xticks(rotation=45)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

# Apply to key relationships
stacked_barplot(data, "Ward_Facility_Code", "Department")
stacked_barplot(data, "Ward_Facility_Code", "Severity of Illness")

def adj_r2_score(predictors, targets, predictions):
    """
    Calculate adjusted R-squared score

    Purpose: Accounts for model complexity by penalizing additional features

    Formula: Adj R² = 1 - ((1 - R²) * (n - 1) / (n - k - 1))
    where n = sample size, k = number of features
    """
    r2 = r2_score(targets, predictions)
    n = predictors.shape[0]  # Number of samples
    k = predictors.shape[1]  # Number of features
    return 1 - ((1 - r2) * (n - 1) / (n - k - 1))

def mape_score(targets, predictions):
    """
    Calculate Mean Absolute Percentage Error

    Purpose: Provides intuitive percentage-based error metric

    Formula: MAPE = (1/n) * Σ(|actual - predicted| / |actual|) * 100
    """
    return np.mean(np.abs((targets - predictions) / targets)) * 100

def model_performance_regression(model, predictors, target):
    """
    Comprehensive model evaluation function

    Parameters:
    model: Trained sklearn model
    predictors (DataFrame): Feature matrix
    target (Series): Target variable

    Returns:
    DataFrame: Performance metrics summary

    Purpose: Standardized evaluation across all algorithms
    """
    # Generate predictions
    pred = model.predict(predictors)

    # Calculate all metrics
    r2 = r2_score(target, pred)
    adjr2 = adj_r2_score(predictors, target, pred)
    rmse = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(target, pred))
    mae = mean_absolute_error(target, pred)
    mape = mape_score(target, pred)

    # Create results dataframe
    df_perf = pd.DataFrame({
        "RMSE": [rmse],
        "MAE": [mae],
        "R-squared": [r2],
        "Adj. R-squared": [adjr2],
        "MAPE": [mape],
    })

    return df_perf

def cross_validate_models(models_dict, X, y, cv_folds=5):
    """
    Perform cross-validation for model stability assessment

    Parameters:
    models_dict (dict): Dictionary of trained models
    X (DataFrame): Feature matrix
    y (Series): Target variable
    cv_folds (int): Number of cross-validation folds

    Returns:
    DataFrame: Cross-validation results
    """
    cv_results = {}

    # Define scoring metrics
    scoring_metrics = {
        'neg_mean_squared_error': 'neg_mean_squared_error',
        'neg_mean_absolute_error': 'neg_mean_absolute_error',
        'r2': 'r2'
    }

    for model_name, model_info in models_dict.items():
        print(f"Cross-validating {model_name}...")
        model = model_info['model']

        # Perform cross-validation for each metric
        cv_scores = {}
        for metric_name, scoring in scoring_metrics.items():
            scores = cross_val_score(model, X, y, cv=cv_folds, scoring=scoring)
            cv_scores[metric_name] = {
                'mean': scores.mean(),
                'std': scores.std(),
                'scores': scores
            }

        cv_results[model_name] = cv_scores

    # Create summary dataframe
    summary_rows = []
    for model_name, scores in cv_results.items():
        row = {
            'Model': model_name,
            'CV_RMSE_mean': np.sqrt(-scores['neg_mean_squared_error']['mean']),
            'CV_RMSE_std': scores['neg_mean_squared_error']['std'],
            'CV_MAE_mean': -scores['neg_mean_absolute_error']['mean'],
            'CV_MAE_std': scores['neg_mean_absolute_error']['std'],
            'CV_R2_mean': scores['r2']['mean'],
            'CV_R2_std': scores['r2']['std']
        }
        summary_rows.append(row)

    cv_summary = pd.DataFrame(summary_rows)
    print("\nCross-Validation Summary:")
    print(cv_summary.round(4))

    return cv_results, cv_summary

# Perform cross-validation
cv_results, cv_summary = cross_validate_models(ensemble_results, X, y)

        ranking = comparison_df[primary_metric].sort_values(ascending=True)

    for i, (model, score) in enumerate(ranking.items(), 1):
        print(f"{i}. {model}: {score:.4f}")

        'RMSE': 'CV_RMSE_mean',
        'MAE': 'CV_MAE_mean',
        'R-squared': 'CV_R2_mean'
    }

    if primary_metric in cv_metric_map:
        cv_metric = cv_metric_map[primary_metric]
        cv_best = cv_summary.loc[cv_summary[cv_metric].idxmax() if 'R2' in cv_metric 
                                else cv_summary[cv_metric].idxmin(), 'Model']
        print(f"\nBest by Cross-Validation {primary_metric}: {cv_best}")

    # Final recommendation

def perform_grid_search_tuning(base_model, param_grid, X_train, y_train, cv_folds=5):
    """
    Comprehensive grid search with detailed reporting

    Parameters:
    base_model: Sklearn model object
    param_grid (dict): Parameter grid for search
    X_train, y_train: Training data
    cv_folds (int): Cross-validation folds

    Returns:
    tuple: (best_model, search_results, tuning_report)
    """
    print("Starting Grid Search Hyperparameter Tuning...")
    print(f"Parameter space size: {np.prod([len(v) for v in param_grid.values()])} combinations")

    # Configure grid search
    grid_search = GridSearchCV(
        estimator=base_model,
        param_grid=param_grid,
        scoring='neg_mean_squared_error',
        cv=cv_folds,
        n_jobs=-1,  # Use all available processors
        verbose=1,   # Progress reporting
        return_train_score=True
    )

    # Perform search
    import time
    start_time = time.time()
    grid_search.fit(X_train, y_train)
    end_time = time.time()

    # Extract best model
    best_model = grid_search.best_estimator_

    # Create detailed report
    tuning_report = {
        'best_params': grid_search.best_params_,
        'best_score': grid_search.best_score_,
        'search_time': end_time - start_time,
        'total_combinations': len(grid_search.cv_results_['params']),
        'best_index': grid_search.best_index_
    }

    print(f"\nTuning completed in {tuning_report['search_time']:.2f} seconds")
    print(f"Best parameters: {tuning_report['best_params']}")
    print(f"Best CV score (neg MSE): {tuning_report['best_score']:.4f}")
    print(f"Best RMSE: {np.sqrt(-tuning_report['best_score']):.4f}")

    return best_model, grid_search, tuning_report

def analyze_hyperparameter_effects(grid_results):
    """
    Analyze the effect of different hyperparameters on model performance

    Parameters:
    grid_results: GridSearchCV results object

    Returns:
    DataFrame: Parameter effect analysis
    """
    # Convert results to DataFrame
    results_df = pd.DataFrame(grid_results.cv_results_)

    # Calculate RMSE from negative MSE
    results_df['mean_rmse'] = np.sqrt(-results_df['mean_test_score'])
    results_df['std_rmse'] = results_df['std_test_score'] / (2 * results_df['mean_rmse'])

    # Analyze parameter effects
    param_effects = {}

    for param in grid_results.param_grid.keys():
        param_col = f'param_{param}'
        if param_col in results_df.columns:
            # Group by parameter value and calculate mean performance
            param_analysis = results_df.groupby(param_col)['mean_rmse'].agg(['mean', 'std', 'count'])
            param_effects[param] = param_analysis

            print(f"\nEffect of {param}:")
            print(param_analysis.round(4))

    # Create visualization
    n_params = len(param_effects)
    if n_params > 0:
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, min(n_params, 3), figsize=(15, 5))
        if n_params == 1:
            axes = [axes]

        for i, (param, effect_data) in enumerate(param_effects.items()):
            if i < 3:  # Limit to 3 plots
                ax = axes[i] if n_params > 1 else axes[0]
                effect_data['mean'].plot(kind='bar', ax=ax, alpha=0.7)
                ax.set_title(f'Effect of {param} on RMSE')
                ax.set_ylabel('Mean RMSE')
                plt.setp(ax.get_xticklabels(), rotation=45)

        plt.tight_layout()
        plt.show()

    return param_effects

# Analyze hyperparameter effects (if grid search was performed)
